test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 10 May, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. 

Before about 1830, _______ sermons, tracts and addresses routinely broached female intemperance.
solution:
The correct answer is** "temperance".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence discusses topics addressed in sermons, tracts, and addresses before 1830.
 
• "Female intemperance" is mentioned, suggesting a theme of moderation or self-restraint, especially related to alcohol consumption.
 
• Only **"temperance" **among the four choices precisely fits this context, as it refers to abstinence from alcohol.

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 2".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Confluence **typically means a place where two rivers or streams join to become one. It can also figuratively mean a situation in which two things come together or happen at the same time. However, it doesn't make sense in the context of the sentence as it doesn't relate to the theme of sermons, tracts, or speeches.
 
• **Temperance** has a historic connection with social and religious movements advocating for moderation or complete abstinence, particularly in alcohol consumption. Hence,** 'temperance sermons'** would be sermons advocating for such moderation or abstinence. It fits in perfectly with the mentioned **"female intemperance".**
 
• Congruence is about agreement or harmony; compatibility. In mathematics, it refers to the quality of being the same in size and shape. It doesn't inherently connect with the idea of sermons, tracts, or addresses, especially ones addressing issues of intemperance.
 
• Affluence means wealth. **'Affluence sermons' **does not make sense in this context as the sentence refers to discussions of** 'female intemperance',** not wealth or prosperity.
